cards.title: Pick an app colour theme: Classic or one of 16 hues
cards.user_does: Opens Appearance and clicks a swatch in the colour theme row.
cards.user_sees: The whole interface recolours to that hue at once, with no restart; Classic keeps the original neutral look.
rules: Classic is the default and sits first; the 16 hued themes follow in colour-wheel order: Ember, Copper, Sand, Moss, Fern, Jade, Teal, Lagoon, Sky, Cobalt, Indigo, Iris, Violet, Orchid, Rose, Graphite.
Graphite carries no colour at all (a greyscale theme).
A missing or unknown theme id is treated as Classic, both on load and when saved.
A live preview next to the swatches shows the selected theme; when nothing is hued the preview falls back to a violet sample.
Pop-out windows use the same colour theme as the main window.
acceptance: Fresh profile → Classic is selected; click Teal → sidebar, top bar and accents turn teal within one frame.
Put an unknown theme id in the settings file and start → app shows Classic and the picker selects Classic.
With Rose selected, open a pop-out window → it is Rose too.
cards.compat: Settings key themeId: 'classic' or one of 16 hue ids; any other value imports as classic.

cards.title: Tint, saturation and depth sliders fine-tune the theme
cards.user_does: Drags the tint, saturation or depth slider under the theme swatches.
cards.user_sees: Tint rotates the hue, saturation strengthens or mutes it, depth makes backgrounds deeper or lighter; the preview and the app update as the slider moves.
rules: Tint runs from −180 to +180 degrees (default 0); saturation from 0 to 160 % (default 100); depth from −3 to +6 steps (default 0).
All three sliders are disabled while Classic is selected.
Out-of-range values are clamped to the range; non-numeric values fall back to the defaults.
acceptance: Select Classic → all three sliders are disabled.
Select Moss, drag saturation to 0 → interface goes grey; back to 100 → Moss returns.
Write saturation 500 into the settings file → app uses 160; write 'abc' → app uses 100.
cards.compat: Settings keys themeHueShift, themeSaturation, themeDepth (numbers, clamped on import).

cards.title: Terminal colours can follow the app theme
cards.user_does: In the terminal colour scheme picker, chooses "Match app theme".
cards.user_sees: Terminal background, foreground and palette are derived from the current app hue, and change whenever the app theme or sliders change.
rules: Match is one entry in the existing terminal picker; the scheme catalog, separate light scheme and imported schemes all remain available.
The reverse direction (app colours derived from a chosen terminal scheme) was proposed as an improvement and never shipped.
acceptance: Choose Match, then switch app theme from Sky to Ember → open terminals recolour without reopening.
Choose a catalog scheme again → terminal stops following the app hue.

cards.title: No flash of the wrong theme or font at startup
cards.user_does: Launches the app or opens another window.
cards.user_sees: The first painted frame already has the saved light/dark mode, colour theme and app font; nothing flips after load.
rules: Mode, colour theme and app font are applied before the first render of every window.
Switching light/dark suppresses CSS transitions for two frames so colours do not animate across the change.
Known gap: the native window background shown before the page loads follows the OS light/dark setting, not the hue.
acceptance: Save Dark + Cobalt + a non-default app font, restart → first frame is dark Cobalt in that font (screen-record at 60 fps, no light frame).
Toggle Light↔Dark → no visible colour fade on panels.

cards.title: Light, Dark or System appearance mode
cards.user_does: Picks System, Light or Dark under Interface.
cards.user_sees: The app switches immediately; with System it follows the OS and changes live when the OS mode changes.
rules: Default is System.
Terminals use a separate light colour scheme in light mode by default; the user can turn that off to keep one scheme in both modes.
acceptance: Mode System, flip the OS to dark while the app runs → app goes dark without restart.
Mode Light with the separate light scheme on → terminals use the light scheme.

cards.title: Settings opens to ten pages plus a small per-repo page
cards.user_does: Presses Mod+Comma, or picks Settings in the app menu (macOS) or File menu (Windows/Linux).
cards.user_sees: A settings view with a sidebar of pages and a list of projects; choosing a page shows its sections.
rules: Pages kept: General, Appearance, Accounts & keys, Agents, Terminal & sessions, Git & worktrees, Safety, Notifications, Shortcuts, Usage; each repo gets one small page.
The old app had 33 fixed sections plus one per repo; everything else is cut or folded (see the D cards of this area).
Sections tied to one platform hide elsewhere (macOS-only, desktop-only).
Links from elsewhere in the app can open Settings at a given page and section; the target is waited for until it renders, then scrolled into view.
The sidebar project list shows each project once; grouping the same project across several hosts went with the dropped remote area.
Pages load lazily so opening Settings stays quick.
The menu entry shows the current Settings shortcut as a hint only.
Settings opens from the app menu (under the app name on macOS, under File elsewhere) and with Mod+Comma.
Closing Settings returns to the screen it was opened from, also when Settings is reopened while already open; opening Settings clears any leftover settings search.
Safety holds the protected-actions rules (area 10) and Usage holds the stats page (area 06); this area owns only their place in the page list.
acceptance: Press Mod+Comma → Settings opens on the last or first page.
Count sidebar pages → exactly the ten named, plus one entry per repo.
Follow an in-app link to the shortcut policy setting → Shortcuts page opens scrolled to it.

cards.title: Search across all settings
cards.user_does: Presses Mod+F inside Settings, or types in the settings search box.
cards.user_sees: Only matching settings remain, across every page; a page whose title matches is ranked first; collapsed sections open to show their matches.
rules: Each setting carries extra plain-language search words, so everyday terms find technical settings.
Section collapse toggles are disabled while a search is active.
Clearing the search restores the previous collapse state.
Agent names, ids and launch commands are searchable; a query that matches only an advanced control reveals that control.
When many projects match a search, only the active page is drawn so typing stays responsive.
Matches of equal rank keep the order they have on their page.
Oversized search text, including a huge run of spaces, is rejected before any trimming or matching, so a giant paste cannot stall the page.
acceptance: Search 'font' → hits from Appearance and Terminal appear; the Appearance sections containing them are expanded.
Search 'shortcuts' → Shortcuts page ranks first.
cards.compat: Keybinding id settings.search (default Mod+F, scope settings).

cards.title: Shortcuts page lists every command with its keys
cards.user_does: Opens Shortcuts, picks a filter or types in the search box.
cards.user_sees: Commands grouped by area with their current chords; filters for all, modified, unassigned and conflicting; badges mark Modified, Unassigned, Disabled and Conflicts.
rules: Search matches command titles, group names, extra keywords, command ids and chords for any platform.
Search input is capped by byte length so very long pastes cannot stall the list.
Each row says whether the command still fires while a terminal has focus or is held back by the terminal policy.
Commands behind an off flag are left out of the list.
acceptance: Filter Unassigned → only commands with no chord show.
Search 'Mod+K' (or its rendered form) → the clear-terminal command shows.

cards.title: Record, add, disable or reset a shortcut
cards.user_does: Clicks a command's chord and presses new keys; or uses add another, remove, disable or reset on the row.
cards.user_sees: A recorder waits for the key combination and saves it; the row updates and the app menu shows the new accelerator.
rules: Esc cancels recording without changing anything.
A command can hold several chords; each can be replaced or removed on its own.
A double-tap of a modifier (for example Shift then Shift) can be recorded as a chord.
Disable leaves the command with no chord and saves that choice; reset restores the shipped default.
Removing the chord being recorded stops recording; removing another chord of the same command keeps recording on the chord the user picked.
Every change is written to the keybindings file at once, broadcast to all windows and rebuilds the app menu.
A double tap counts only when the second press of the same modifier lands within about 300 ms, with no other key in between, no other modifier held, and not from key auto-repeat.
A chord needs a modifier other than Shift; Shift-only chords are refused, except that the terminal command that switches the OS input source accepts Shift+Space.
acceptance: Record Mod+Shift+K on a command → row shows it, badge Modified, file contains the entry.
Press Esc while recording → previous chord stays.
Reset → default chord returns and Modified badge clears.

cards.title: Shortcut conflicts are flagged, scope by scope
cards.user_does: Records a chord that another command already uses, or hand-edits the file into a clash.
cards.user_sees: Both rows carry a Conflicts badge and appear under the conflicts filter; on macOS a warning appears when the OS captures the chord (Mission Control desktop switching).
rules: Conflicts are judged per scope: global, tabs, terminal, browser, editor, file explorer, composer, settings; the same chord in two non-overlapping scopes is fine.
Clashes with native menu accelerators count as conflicts.
When a hand edit to the file creates a clash, the conflicting override is ignored and a diagnostic is shown.
Unassigned commands never conflict.
A conflicting row shows a short fix-it hint, worded the same however many commands clash, wrapped in full rather than cut off.
The new-tab-with-agent commands of agents turned off on the Agents page never count as conflicts.
The macOS desktop-switching warning appears only when the current keyboard layout really types a digit on that key; otherwise it stays silent.
acceptance: Bind Mod+P to a second global command → both rows show Conflicts.
macOS with Ctrl+digit desktop switching on → binding Ctrl+2 shows the OS-capture warning.

cards.title: Shortcuts live in a user-owned file, ~/.kolux/keybindings.json
cards.user_does: Edits ~/.kolux/keybindings.json by hand, or lets the Shortcuts page write it.
cards.user_sees: Overrides in the file take effect after a page edit or a manual reload; the file survives upgrades.
rules: The file holds a version number (1), a map of command id to chord, and optional per-platform sections for macOS, Linux and Windows.
A chord value may be one string, a list of strings, or null/false meaning deliberately unbound.
Entries in the active platform section win over the common map.
Overrides written at the top level by older builds are accepted and moved into the map.
An unreadable or invalid file shows an error, falls back to defaults and is never overwritten.
The file is created empty when missing; every write goes through a temp file so a crash cannot leave half a file.
Shortcut overrides kept in the old settings store are migrated once, only when no file exists yet.
On upgrade, users whose tab-switch keys changed between versions get their old chords pinned in the file so muscle memory keeps working; this runs once and retries next launch if the write failed.
Saving from the page writes the active platform's overrides into that platform's section and leaves the other platforms' sections untouched.

The one-time pin of the old tab-switch chords is judged per platform: an override saved for another platform does not stop the active platform from being pinned, other overrides are left intact, and running it again changes nothing.
acceptance: Write {"version":1,"keybindings":{"terminal.clear":null}} and reload → clear-terminal shows Unassigned.
Corrupt the JSON and reload → error diagnostic, default chords active, file contents unchanged on disk.
Add a win32 section overriding a common entry → on Windows the platform value applies.
cards.compat: ~/.kolux/keybindings.json: { "$schema"?, "version": 1, "keybindings": { "<command id>": "chord" | ["chord", ...] | null | false }, "platforms": { "darwin": {}, "linux": {}, "win32": {} } }. Import must keep every override and the null/false meaning.

cards.title: Open, reveal or reload the keybindings file from Settings
cards.user_does: Opens the file menu on the Shortcuts page.
cards.user_sees: Choices to edit the file inside the app, open it in an installed editor or the default app, reveal it in the file manager, or "Reload from Disk".
rules: Editor choices come from the configured open-in applications.
Reload re-reads the file and broadcasts the result to every window; no automatic file watching was found, so hand edits wait for reload.
If the file is missing it is created before opening.
acceptance: Edit the file outside the app, click Reload from Disk → the new chord shows in the list and the menu.
Reveal → file manager opens at ~/.kolux with the file selected.

cards.title: Shipped default shortcuts, and the commands left unbound
cards.user_does: Uses the app on a fresh install.
cards.user_sees: Core commands have chords out of the box, differing by platform where the OS reserves keys; many newer commands ship with no chord until the user assigns one.
rules: Of 129 commands, 78 ship bound and 51 ship unbound (including one 'new tab with agent X' command per supported agent).
Mod means Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere.
Some commands exist with a default only on macOS (rename workspace, rename tab, new agent tab, ports panel, maximize floating workspace).
The agent-per-tab commands are generated from the agent list, one per agent.

The full default table (command id with its macOS, Linux and Windows chords, and which ship unbound) is carried from the keybindings registry; command ids are user-facing because they are the keys of the keybindings file.
Add a Session and Remove a Session ship unbound; Ctrl+Shift+N stays with Create worktree.
acceptance: Fresh profile on Windows → Alt+1 selects tab 1, Ctrl+Shift+J opens the palette, Mod+Shift+D splits right.
Fresh profile → filter Unassigned lists the board, dashboard, tasks, inbox and floor views.
cards.compat: Bound defaults (macOS | Windows/Linux): worktree.quickOpen Mod+P; app.settings Mod+Comma; app.forceReload Mod+Shift+R; worktree.palette Mod+J | Mod+Shift+J; workspace.create Mod+N | Mod+Shift+N; workspace.delete Mod+Shift+Backspace; workspace.selectByIndex Mod+1..9; sidebar.left.toggle Mod+B; sidebar.right.toggle Mod+L; zoom.in Mod+Equal, Mod+Shift+Plus, Mod+NumpadAdd; zoom.out Mod+Minus, Mod+NumpadSubtract; zoom.reset Mod+0; sidebar.focusWorktreeList Mod+Shift+0; tab.previousRecent Ctrl+Tab; tab.selectByIndex Ctrl+1..9 | Alt+1..9; settings.search Mod+F; terminal.splitRight Mod+D | Mod+Shift+D; terminal.splitDown Mod+Shift+D | Alt+Shift+D; terminal.clear Mod+K; view.cycleWorkspaceView Mod+Alt+V; terminals.focusNextNeedsYou Mod+Shift+J | Ctrl+J; macOS only: workspace.rename Mod+Alt+R, tab.rename Mod+R, tab.newAgent Mod+Alt+T, sidebar.ports.toggle Mod+Shift+I. Unbound ids: workspace.openBoard, dashboard.toggle, view.tasks, view.inbox, view.floor, sidebar.checks.toggle, sidebar.sleepingWorkspaces.toggle, floatingWorkspace.minimize, tab.openQuickCommandsMenu, sourceControl.sendReviewNotes, terminal.equalizePaneSizes, terminal.setTitle, terminal.clearPaneTitle, terminal.switchInputSource, sessions.add, sessions.remove, tab.newAgent.<agent>.

cards.title: Choose whether app or terminal gets shortcuts first
cards.user_does: On Shortcuts, picks "Kolux first" or "Terminal first".
cards.user_sees: Kolux first (default): app shortcuts keep working while typing in a terminal. Terminal first: only commands marked safe for terminals fire; every other chord goes to the program in the terminal.
rules: The per-row terminal status on the Shortcuts page updates when the policy changes.
The policy applies to every terminal pane, including the floating terminal.
acceptance: Terminal first, focus a terminal running a TUI, press Mod+P → the TUI receives it; quick open does not appear.
Kolux first → Mod+P opens quick open even with a terminal focused.

cards.title: Tab and workspace switching keys adapt to platform and layout
cards.user_does: Presses tab-by-number, workspace-by-number or Ctrl+Tab.
cards.user_sees: The right tab or workspace activates; Ctrl+Tab goes to the most recently used tab by default.
rules: Tab-by-number is Ctrl+digit on macOS and Alt+digit on Windows/Linux; workspace-by-number is Mod+digit.
Ctrl+Tab order can be most-recent (default) or left-to-right position.
Digit and punctuation chords match the physical key so non-US layouts still work.
Window-level shortcuts are resolved before page focus, so they work from any panel.

Fresh installs: Mod+Shift+[ and Mod+Shift+] cycle through all tabs, Mod+Alt+[ and Mod+Alt+] cycle through tabs of the same kind; installs upgraded from before this pairing keep the reverse pairing they learned (pinned in the keybindings file).
acceptance: Windows: Alt+3 → third tab.
Visit tabs 1, 3, 2, then Ctrl+Tab → tab 3 (most recent order).

cards.title: Appearance page in three collapsible sections
cards.user_does: Opens Appearance and collapses or expands sections.
cards.user_sees: Interface, Terminal, and Window & Sidebar sections, all open by default; a collapsed section shows a one-line summary of its current values; the app icon picker sits at the bottom.
rules: A link to a specific appearance setting opens its section and scrolls to it.
Search reopens any section that holds a match.
A deep link reopens only its target section; the other sections keep whatever collapse state they had.
acceptance: Collapse Terminal → its header summarises font and scheme.
Follow a link to the sidebar look setting while Window & Sidebar is collapsed → it expands and scrolls.

cards.title: Interface language with English fallback
cards.user_does: Picks a language under Interface.
cards.user_sees: Menus, settings and screens switch to that language; dates, relative times and weekday names follow it.
rules: Choices: System (default), English, Simplified Chinese, Korean, Japanese, Spanish, French.
System picks the OS language when supported; unsupported OS languages, including Traditional Chinese, fall back to English.
Language catalogs load on demand; any missing string shows in English.
Native menus from the main process switch language too.
Lists sort with the language's own collation.
Interface copy is guarded against developer jargon in every language (plain-language rule for business users).
An unknown saved language value falls back to System.
The saved language is applied as soon as settings finish loading.
Product and provider names inside labels stay untranslated.
Settings search finds the language setting by each language's own name (for example Français) whatever language the interface is in.
acceptance: Pick Japanese → menus and settings in Japanese; relative times read in Japanese.
OS set to Traditional Chinese, language System → English.

cards.title: Choose the app font and the editor font
cards.user_does: Types or picks a font family for the interface and for the code editor.
cards.user_sees: Suggestions from fonts installed on the machine as they type; the chosen font applies at once.
rules: Installed fonts are listed from the OS (on Windows through PowerShell), with a built-in fallback list if that fails.
A safe fallback stack is appended to any chosen family so text never disappears.
Leaving the field empty returns to the default font.
Installed fonts are looked up only once the user opens a font picker.
Suggestions rank names that start with the typed text before names that merely contain it.
An empty editor font means the editor follows the terminal font.
Focusing a font field that already holds a chosen font shows the full suggestion list, not just names matching the current value.
acceptance: Type 'Cas' → installed Cascadia variants suggested; pick one → interface font changes.
Enter a font that is not installed → text still renders in the fallback.

cards.title: Zoom the whole interface in and out
cards.user_does: Presses Mod+= or Mod+-, Mod+0 to reset, uses the View menu, or the zoom control under Interface.
cards.user_sees: All text and controls scale together; the level is remembered across restarts.
rules: Each step is half a zoom level (about 9.5 % larger or smaller; one full level is a factor of 1.2).
On macOS the window buttons are re-aligned to the zoomed title bar.
The zoom control has a reset button.
Zoom is clamped between -3 levels (about 58 %) and +5 levels (about 249 %); reset returns to 100 % from any level.
The View menu offers Zoom In, Zoom Out and Reset Size.
acceptance: Press Mod+= twice → interface about 44 % larger; restart → same size.
Press Mod+0 → normal size.

cards.title: Show or hide title, toolbar buttons and status bar items
cards.user_does: Toggles items under Window & Sidebar, or ticks them in View › Appearance.
cards.user_sees: The app name in the title bar, the Tasks and Automations buttons, and the status bar or its individual indicators appear or disappear immediately.
rules: Defaults: app name shown, Tasks button shown, Automations button hidden, status bar shown.
Menu checkmarks and the settings toggles stay in sync; changing Automations visibility rebuilds the menu.
Usage can be shown as amount used or amount remaining.
Claude/Codex usage indicators were removed from the status bar on 2026-10-05 (usage now sits top right); which status bar items remain is to be confirmed.

The View menu has an Appearance submenu with Toggle Left Sidebar, Toggle Right Sidebar and checkboxes for the status bar, Tasks button, Automations button and titlebar app name; its mobile-button checkbox goes with the dropped mobile feature.
acceptance: Untick Show Tasks Button in the View menu → button disappears and the setting toggle turns off.
Toggle Show Titlebar App Name off → title bar shows no name.

cards.title: Left sidebar look and worktree card density
cards.user_does: Picks a sidebar look and a card layout under Window & Sidebar.
cards.user_sees: The left sidebar uses the default surface, matches the terminal background, or takes a chosen tint; worktree cards show as Default, Compact or Detailed.
rules: Tinted mode adds a colour picker and a strength control.
Pinned worktrees can also be listed inside their groups (off by default).
Git-ignored files can be shown or hidden in the file explorer (shown by default).
acceptance: Choose Tinted, pick red at low strength → sidebar gets a faint red wash.
Choose Compact → worktree cards lose their second line.

cards.title: Terminal text, cursor and rendering
cards.user_does: Adjusts font size, family, weight, line height, cursor, ligatures, GPU use and contrast under Terminal.
cards.user_sees: A live preview terminal in the page and all open terminals update.
rules: Font size defaults to 14 with minus/plus steppers and typed values.
Line height defaults to 1; cursor defaults to a blinking block; ligatures and GPU acceleration default to automatic.
A minimum-contrast mode keeps text readable on any scheme.
The preview runs a real, short-lived terminal that is closed when the page is left.
Invalid line heights are normalised on save.
Terminal font family and normal and bold weights are chosen on the same page (font behaviour is detailed in area 03).
Terminal font size runs from 10 to 24 in steps of 1; the minus stepper is disabled at 10 and the plus stepper at 24.
acceptance: Click + on font size → preview and open terminals grow by one point.
Set cursor to bar, blink off → all terminals show a steady bar.

cards.title: Terminal colour schemes for dark and light
cards.user_does: Searches the scheme catalog and picks one for dark mode and one for light mode.
cards.user_sees: Terminals switch scheme with the app mode; pane dividers and inactive-pane dimming follow the choices.
rules: Default dark scheme is the app's own dark scheme; a separate light scheme is on by default with a Tango-style light scheme.
Divider colour is set per mode; divider thickness defaults to 3 px.
Inactive panes are dimmed with a configurable opacity and a 140 ms fade.
The catalog filters as the user types.
Custom schemes are stored in settings and normalised on load.
acceptance: Pick different dark and light schemes, flip app mode → terminals swap schemes.
Focus another pane → the previous one dims over about 140 ms.

cards.title: Import terminal schemes from Warp and Ghostty
cards.user_does: Imports a Warp YAML theme file, or imports from an existing Ghostty config.
cards.user_sees: The scheme joins the custom list; the Ghostty import shows a preview of what will change before applying.
rules: Invalid files show an error and import nothing.
The number of custom schemes is capped; importing past the cap is refused with a message.
Cancelling the file picker leaves the import dialog closed.
When the Ghostty config already matches the current settings, the preview says so and there is nothing to apply.

Warp import previews on click, reading Warp's own themes folder or a theme file the user picks; the user ticks which schemes to bring in (with a select-all), nothing is applied when none is ticked, and replacing an existing scheme is allowed even at the cap.
acceptance: Import a valid Warp YAML → new custom scheme selectable.
Import a broken file → error, list unchanged.
cards.compat: Warp theme YAML and Ghostty config as import sources.

cards.title: Terminal input, clipboard and scrolling behaviour
cards.user_does: Changes scrollback, copy and paste, mouse and keyboard options under Terminal & sessions.
cards.user_sees: Terminals keep the chosen history length and react to mouse and clipboard as configured.
rules: Scrollback is set in rows; out-of-range values are normalised and older settings are migrated to rows.
Copy on select is off by default; right-click paste and middle-click paste are options (middle-click moved here from the removed Input page).
Programs in the terminal may write the clipboard (OSC 52), on by default.
Hide mouse while typing and focus follows mouse are off by default.
Scroll sensitivity, fast-scroll multiplier and TUI scroll speed are adjustable.
macOS: Option can act as Alt (automatic by default); Japanese keyboards can map the Yen key to backslash (off).
Middle-click paste of the primary selection is on by default on Linux and macOS and opt-in on Windows; right-click paste follows the platform convention (on for Windows).
acceptance: Set scrollback to 1000 rows → scrolling stops after about 1000 lines.
Turn copy on select on → selecting text puts it on the clipboard.

cards.title: Pick the default shell on Windows
cards.user_does: On Windows, picks the shell new terminals start in.
cards.user_sees: New terminals open in Windows PowerShell (default), PowerShell 7 when installed, Git Bash, or a WSL shell.
rules: The setting only appears on Windows.
A PowerShell version choice (automatic by default) prefers the newer PowerShell when present.
A WSL shell here is just a local terminal; running agents inside WSL is part of the dropped remote area.
Git Bash is offered only when it is found on the machine.
An older per-terminal WSL distribution setting is no longer offered on Windows.
acceptance: With pwsh installed, choose PowerShell 7 → new tab runs pwsh.
macOS → setting absent.

cards.title: Agents page: which agents, the default, and how they launch
cards.user_does: Turns agents on or off, picks the default agent, and sets launch options.
cards.user_sees: Only enabled, installed agents are offered elsewhere in the app; new sessions use the default agent and its options.
rules: Disabling the default agent clears the default.
Refresh re-detects installed agent CLIs; a detection that finds none never erases the saved default.
Per agent: command override, default arguments and default environment variables, edited as drafts that save on blur.
Toggles: status hooks (on), auto-generated tab titles (off), 200k context cap with auto-compact (on), keep the computer awake while agents run (off, with modes).
Agents not signed in link to their sign-in on Accounts & keys.

Agent Permissions: Yolo (default: agents start with the flags that skip permission prompts where their CLI has them) or Manual (agents ask before changing things); agents whose launch arguments were overridden are not affected, and a mixed state shows as Yolo. Since 2026-10-05 Claude starts in its automatic permission mode by default.
Keep-awake has On, Agent (only while an agent is working) and Off; the help text describes lid-close behaviour according to the device and its power settings.

Sign-in from the Agents page: Claude and Codex open their browser sign-in on Accounts & keys; any other agent starts in the current workspace with no prompt and the screen switches to its terminal so the user signs in there.
That in-terminal sign-in needs an open workspace; when there is none, or the launch fails, Settings stays open and nothing else changes.
When detection finds no agents, the saved default is still listed and marked as saved but not detected right now, Auto is not shown as the active choice, and Refresh stays reachable.
On load, a saved permission-skipping default argument is removed for an agent whose CLI does not accept it, so that agent still starts; arguments an agent does accept are kept.
acceptance: Disable the current default → default shows none; new session asks or uses first available.
Uninstall every agent CLI and Refresh → saved default still set once one is reinstalled.
cards.compat: Settings keys defaultTuiAgent, disabledTuiAgents, agentCmdOverrides, agentDefaultArgs, agentDefaultEnv.

cards.title: Model and effort per tier for orchestration workers
cards.user_does: On the Agents page, picks a provider, then a model and effort level for each worker tier.
cards.user_sees: When a coordinator assigns a tier to a task, the worker launches with that tier's model on the same provider.
rules: Each tier can be left unset, which means the provider's default.
Effort choices depend on the chosen model; changing the model keeps the effort when still valid, otherwise resets it.
Only providers that support routing are listed.
acceptance: Set the fast tier to a small model, start an orchestrated task that uses that tier → worker header shows the small model.
Switch to a model without effort levels → the effort picker disappears.

cards.title: Install the command-line tool from Settings
cards.user_does: Clicks the install or register action for the command-line tool.
cards.user_sees: The tool is put on the PATH, or a clear reason is shown when the OS refused or the install failed.
rules: A refusal (user cancelled an elevation prompt) and a failure are reported differently.
Agent skill setup panels show whether each agent's helper is installed and re-check when the page regains focus.
A skill setup panel re-checks once when its install command finishes and its terminal exits.
On Windows a missing runtime choice is treated as the local Windows host.

Each skill setup panel runs its install in an inline terminal; a failed run shows Setup failed with the exit code, keeps the terminal visible and offers Retry in a fresh terminal; the notice clears only after a later run succeeds.
Once installed, the panel shows Installed with an Update button instead of the install label.
On Windows the copyable install command fits the configured default shell: cmd-family shells get a guarded form that first checks the package runner is present, Git Bash gets the bare command.
When the system gives no detail for a failed command-line install, a generic reason is shown; a reason the installer did give is shown as given, not reworded.
acceptance: Install on a machine without the tool → new shell finds the command.
Cancel the OS prompt → message says it was cancelled, not failed.

cards.title: Accounts & keys page warns about sign-in problems
cards.user_does: Opens Accounts & keys.
cards.user_sees: Each provider account shows whether it is signed in and usable, with a warning when sign-in is broken or the local config is out of sync.

Rate-limit panels show only accounts that belong to the current view.
Limit auto-resume (Claude continues after its limit resets) is an opt-in toggle, off by default.
A Codex helper that quits because of bad launch arguments is not reported as needing sign-in again.
acceptance: Sign Claude out in its CLI → page shows the Claude sign-in warning.
Turn on auto-resume → setting persists after restart.

cards.title: Git & worktrees page: branch naming and source control defaults
cards.user_does: Sets the branch prefix, rename and base-branch options, and source control view defaults.
cards.user_sees: A live example of the next branch name, with a warning when the prefix would make an invalid branch.
rules: Prefix choices: the git user name (default), a custom text, or none.
Branches are renamed from the work done by default.
Refreshing the local base branch before creating a worktree is off by default.

A Default Compare Base choice sets what each worktree's Git panel compares against: Repository default (the default) or Branch upstream; the source control view defaults to a list, with a set group order.
AI help for commit messages and other source control actions is configured here (agent and instructions).
A prefix made only of slashes collapses to no prefix, and the page says so.
A saved commit-message agent that cannot run the chosen recipe is flagged, with the supported agents listed.
With the commit-message helper set to follow the default agent, its recipe editor stays available even when the default agent is one the helper cannot use directly.
Each source control AI action's extra-arguments field shows an example suited to the agent chosen for that action; when the action follows the default agent, the example follows the default agent.
acceptance: Custom prefix 'tx' → preview shows tx/<name>.
Custom prefix with a space → warning shown, value not applied to new branches.

cards.title: Choose where worktrees are created
cards.user_does: Types or browses to a workspaces folder, or sets KOLUX_WORKSPACES_DIR.
cards.user_sees: New worktrees are created under that folder, nested per repo by default.
rules: Enter saves, Escape reverts, and typing through an input method does not save mid-word.
Recently used folders are remembered.
The environment variable sets the folder without using the page.
Worktrees created outside the app are hidden by default; this can be changed globally and per repo.

Visibility of worktrees made outside the app is set per source: those made by Claude Code, by GSD, in other locations, and custom root folders the user adds (a new custom root starts hidden); changing the global default never rewrites per-repo choices.
Leaving the field submits the typed folder again even when it equals the last attempt, so a failed save can be retried.
acceptance: Browse to D:/wt → next worktree lands in D:/wt/<repo>/<name>.
Start with KOLUX_WORKSPACES_DIR set → new worktrees go there.
cards.compat: Environment variable KOLUX_WORKSPACES_DIR; settings keys workspaceDir, nestWorkspaces.

cards.title: Per-repo page: base branch, setup script, folder
cards.user_does: Opens a repo under the settings project list.
cards.user_sees: The repo's base branch, the setup script that runs in new worktrees, and the folder its worktrees go to.
rules: The setup script opens in a new tab by default.
Visibility of externally created worktrees can be overridden per repo.
Text fields save as drafts and handle input-method composition.
The page also carries the repo's display name (a draft field that keeps input-method composition, for example Hangul typed slowly) and its icon (icon choice is area 01).
Per-repo fields show the inherited global value until the user overrides it; just viewing writes nothing to the repo.
A draft is not saved on blur or close when nothing was edited.
The setup section also sets whether the agent waits for setup to finish, and whether the local setup, the shared one from the repo, or both run; when both exist the page suggests Run both.
acceptance: Set a setup script, create a worktree → script runs in a new tab.
Change base branch to develop → next worktree branches from develop.

cards.user_sees: A sample notification and sound play; a link opens the OS notification settings.
rules: Volume applies to all app sounds.

acceptance: Click test → system notification appears with the chosen sound.

cards.title: Settings save instantly, sync across windows, never expose secrets
cards.user_does: Changes any setting, with more than one window open.
cards.user_sees: The change applies immediately in every window and survives restart.
rules: Secret values are stripped before settings reach page code, both on read and in change broadcasts.
Values are normalised on save and load (scrollback rows, line height, custom schemes, proxy, app icon).
Keys from retired features are dropped on load; older value formats are migrated.
Settings load before the first window paints, so pages never show defaults then jump.
After a save, each window adopts the value the settings store actually kept.
Updates aimed at retired settings are ignored, and their stale values are removed on the next save.
A failed save is logged and does not break the page.
A change made while settings are still loading is kept; the late-arriving load never overwrites it.
A failed save of one setting never undoes another setting that already saved successfully.
acceptance: Change terminal font in window A → window B updates without reload.
Inspect settings delivered to a page → no token or key values present.
cards.compat: Settings file is a data category the importer must carry (key names as in the settings registry).

cards.title: Typed settings fields keep what was typed
cards.user_does: Types in a text or number field and moves on, presses Enter, switches page or closes the window.
cards.user_sees: The value is saved in every case; nothing typed is lost.
rules: Fields save after a short pause, and immediately on leaving the field, page change, or window close.
Input-method composition (Chinese, Japanese, Korean) is not committed mid-word.
Clearable number fields return to their default when emptied.
Unavailable options in segmented controls are shown disabled with the reason.
Long option lists (fonts, schemes) filter as the user types.
Cmd/Ctrl+Enter submits the current form or dialog.
Oversized search text in font and scheme pickers is rejected before any filtering.
A keystroke typed while the previous save is still in flight is kept.
Cmd/Ctrl+Enter is ignored while an input method is composing.
If saving a typed value fails, the typed text stays in the field so it can be saved again.
Saves queued in quick succession are applied in order, each on top of the previous saved result, so no earlier change is lost.
acceptance: Type a proxy URL and close the window within a second → value present after restart.
Compose Japanese in a field → no save until the composition ends.

cards.user_sees: The New look shows the redesigned screens; Classic keeps the older layout.
rules: Profiles that existed before the redesign stay on Classic until switched; the redesign is reached by choosing New.
The default view setting has no effect while Classic is selected.
The View menu has a radio group to switch between Agents, Board and Terminals; Mod+Alt+V cycles them.

With the Classic look the default-screen choice shows only Terminals selected; Agents and Board are disabled with a hint to switch the look to New.

Default view Board, restart with New → Board shows first.

cards.user_sees: The built-in editor and diff views follow those preferences.
rules: Defaults: auto-save off (with a delay once on), minimap off, word wrap on, spellcheck in rich markdown on.
Diffs open inline by default, without word wrap and with whitespace changes hidden.
The combined diff's file tree is hidden by default.
Editor word wrap and diff word wrap are separate choices; changing one never changes the other.
acceptance: Turn auto-save on with 1000 ms → edits save a second after typing stops.
Show whitespace on → whitespace-only changes appear in diffs.

acceptance: Add a preset editor → it appears in a worktree's Open in menu.

acceptance: Set a proxy, check for updates → request reaches the proxy.

acceptance: Pick Blue → dock/taskbar icon turns blue without restart.
Turn minimise to tray on, close the window → app stays in the tray.

cards.title: End every terminal session at once
cards.user_does: Uses the kill-all action for terminal sessions.
cards.user_sees: Every running terminal ends and its pane closes or shows as ended.
rules: Only terminals that existed at the moment of the click are ended; ones opened during the action survive.
Background session state is cleaned up afterwards.

The Manage Sessions section on the Terminal page, offered on every platform, lists the running terminal sessions with Refresh and, per row, Go to terminal and Kill session; Kill all sessions asks first.
Kill all leaves the background terminal service running, so new terminals open straight away; restarting that service is its own action (D-17-060).
Kill all reports success once the terminal tabs are closed, even when the background service had no sessions left to end.
acceptance: Three terminals running, kill all → all three end; a new terminal opens normally afterwards.

cards.title: Optional prompt cache countdown after a Claude agent goes idle
cards.user_does: Turns on the cache timer on the Agents page, picks its duration, then leaves a Claude session idle.
cards.user_sees: The worktree's sidebar card shows a minutes:seconds countdown that turns yellow in the last minute and becomes a red icon when it runs out, whose tooltip says the next message will resend the whole conversation uncached.
rules: Off by default; duration choices are 5 minutes (default) and 1 hour, meant to match the provider's cache lifetime.
Only Claude agents start the countdown, and it starts when the agent goes idle.
With several Claude tabs in one worktree, the card shows the one closest to expiring.
Turning the timer off hides every countdown at once.
acceptance: Timer on at 5 minutes, a Claude session finishes → its card counts down from 5:00; at 0:59 it turns yellow; at 0:00 a red icon with an explanatory tooltip replaces the numbers.
Two Claude tabs in one worktree go idle a minute apart → the card shows the shorter remaining time.
Turn the timer off → all countdowns disappear.

cards.title: Restart the background terminal service
cards.user_does: Chooses Restart daemon in Manage Sessions on the Terminal page, or from the resource usage popover, and confirms.
cards.user_sees: A confirmation warns that every running terminal pane will be killed; after confirming, the panes show their process exited and can be reopened at once, and a toast says whether the restart worked.
rules: Nothing happens until the user confirms; the action cannot be undone.
Sessions still running under an older app version's protocol are preserved.
A failed restart shows an error pointing to the logs; the app itself keeps running.
acceptance: Two terminals running → Restart daemon → confirm → both panes show their process exited; reopening one starts a fresh shell immediately and a success toast appears.
Open the confirmation and cancel → every terminal keeps running.

cards.title: Mouse wheel scrolls long pickers and menus, even inside dialogs
cards.user_does: Opens a long picker or filter menu (labels, assignees, palette filters, workspace cleanup filters, new-workspace sources), often from inside a dialog, and scrolls with the mouse wheel or trackpad.
cards.user_sees: The list under the pointer scrolls; the dialog or page behind it stays still, and a footer pinned under the list stays in place.
rules: The wheel scrolls the nearest part of the menu, between the pointer and the menu's edge, that can still scroll vertically; when the menu itself is the scroller, the menu scrolls.
Parts that only scroll sideways, or that clip their content without scrolling, are skipped.
When nothing in the menu can scroll further, the wheel is left alone and nothing behind the menu jumps.
A control inside the menu that handles the wheel itself keeps priority.
acceptance: Open the GitHub label picker inside the item dialog with more labels than fit → wheel down scrolls the label list; the dialog does not move.
Open the workspace cleanup Filters menu → wheel scrolls the filter list while its footer stays pinned.
Open a short menu that fits without scrolling → wheel changes nothing visible.

cards.title: macOS warns when terminal commands lose the app's permission grants
cards.user_does: Updates or moves the app on macOS while the background terminal service keeps running from the old copy, then opens Kolux or the Manage Sessions part of Settings.
cards.user_sees: A warning that macOS permissions (Accessibility, Automation, protected files) may not reach commands run in Kolux terminals, explaining that restarting the terminal service fixes it and closes running terminals; app-wide it appears as a lasting notice with Open Manage Sessions and Dismiss.
rules: macOS only; shown only while the service is known to be running from an app copy that no longer exists.
If the app cannot tell whether the service is affected, no warning is shown.
The app-wide notice appears at most once per app session; it is checked again when the window regains focus and is withdrawn if the problem has cleared.
Open Manage Sessions clears any settings search and opens Settings at the Manage Sessions part of Terminal & sessions.

Inside Manage Sessions the same warning sits above the session list without the navigation button; after the service is restarted from there (D-17-060) the warning is re-checked and disappears once fixed.
acceptance: On macOS, run terminals from an old app copy, update the app, open it → one warning notice with Open Manage Sessions appears; refocusing the window does not show a second one.
Click Open Manage Sessions → Settings opens on the Manage Sessions part with the warning shown and no navigation button.
Restart the terminal service from Manage Sessions → the warning disappears.
On Windows or Linux → no such warning ever appears.

notes: Registry has 34 settings sections (33 fixed plus one dynamic per-repo), and 'general' is both a kept page and listed among folded sections; treated as kept General absorbing the folded ones.
No file watcher for ~/.kolux/keybindings.json was found; hand edits apply only after the page's reload action.
UI zoom step is 1.2x per level, but the min/max zoom level was not found in source; UNKNOWN.
Native window background before page load follows OS light/dark, not the colour hue (known gap from HANDOFF).
Status bar usage indicators were removed 2026-10-05; the Used/Remaining display choice may now apply only to the top-right usage.
Overlaps: provider cards with area 11, account warnings with 07, agent launch options with 02, repo icon and worktree visibility with 01.
Evidence lines into dumps/tests point at the area dump file; source line numbers come from registry rows.
Round 1 critic: zoom range resolved (half-level steps, clamped -3..+5 levels), replacing the UNKNOWN rule on D-17-019.
Round 1 critic: prompt cache timer was left uncarded by both area 01 and area 06 (each pointed to the other); carded here as D-17-059 because its switch is on the Agents settings page.
Round 1 critic: per-repo Source Control AI override (area 11, D-11-019) sits outside the kept per-repo list of base branch, setup script and folder; flagged for area 11 / DECISIONS.
Round 2 critic: D-17-006 rule on per-host project grouping rewritten (hosts went with area 18); D-17-009 rule on removal during recording corrected (only removing the recorded chord stops recording).
Round 2 critic: wheel scrolling in popover menus (UI primitive folder, mapped to 17 by prefix) was uncarded anywhere; carded as D-17-061 with related 01, 05, 11.
Round 2 critic: Agents-page sign-in for non-Claude/Codex agents launches the agent in the current workspace terminal; not carded in area 07, rule added to D-17-027.

Round 3 critic: macOS warning that the terminal service runs from a removed app copy (permission grants no longer reach terminals) was uncarded in 03, 17 and 19; carded as D-17-062 (its banner sits in Manage Sessions; the auto-replace of an idle host is D-03-108).
Round 3 critic: D-17-027 raised P1 -> P0 and live-unverified -> live (2026-10-05 HANDOFF entries name its Claude auto permission default and the 200k cap toggle).

Round 3 critic: tier/theme tension left for the priorities stage: D-17-031, D-17-033 (pushed 2), D-17-034 (pushed 3) and D-17-059 (pushed 4) carry a top-5 theme but stay P1/P2 as settings for, or polish on, a P0 feature.

Round 3 critic: generic save behaviours seen in Source Control AI settings tests (draft kept on failed save, ordered save queue, no rollback of a successful save) added to D-17-035/D-17-036; the recipes themselves stay with area 11 (D-11-018, D-11-019).
